sources.title: Enterprise managed permissions for GitHub Copilot agent operations
Control GitHub Actions cache access with cache-mode
Block pull requests with exposed secrets from merging
Remediate Code Quality findings with agentic autofix
[Launched] Generally Available: Azure Copilot Troubleshooting Agent
[Launched] Generally Available: Azure Developer CLI (azd) Extension Framework
Azure DevOps Blog (homepage listing, no in-window posts found)
Visual Studio Code September 2026 (version 1.137) release notes

claims.claim: GitHub Copilot enterprise managed permissions for agent operations are generally available for GitHub Copilot Business and GitHub Copilot Enterprise administrators as of 9 September 2026.
Managed permissions cover shell commands, file reads and edits, and network domains, and can be set to blocked, human-approval-required, or auto-allowed.
Managed restrictions cannot be weakened by user or workspace settings, auto-approval, or previously saved approvals.
These controls apply across the GitHub Copilot app, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Visual Studio Code sessions using Agent Host.

cache-mode lets GitHub Actions workflows or jobs apply least-privilege cache access (read, write, write-only) and is generally available on all plans as of 10 September 2026, helping prevent cache poisoning.
A new repository ruleset rule blocks pull requests introducing exposed secrets from merging, complementing existing push protection, announced 9 September 2026.

The Azure Copilot Troubleshooting Agent is a unified, built-in Azure Copilot capability for investigating and resolving operational issues, generally available as of 10 September 2026 via Azure Copilot and Azure Support.
The Azure Developer CLI (azd) Extension Framework is generally available as of 8 September 2026, enabling custom capability extensions for azd.
No Azure DevOps Blog post published in the 7-13 September 2026 reporting window was found; the closest recent posts were dated between 26 and 31 August 2026.
Treating managed permissions, cache-mode, and merge-time secret blocking as a coordinated hardening effort for the same reporting week is an editorial interpretation, not a claim made by GitHub.

Enterprises should treat managed permissions as a prerequisite for expanding Copilot agent mode beyond a small pilot group, and should map agent operations to existing risk/control categories before rollout.
